title: Hang a server's tool-less sliding rail in a 4-post rack: back end into the marked U, then draw out the front and seat it
instruction: Hang the rail on the marked U, back end first, then the front, then let go.
context: Racking servers is core data-centre work. Following a tool-less rail's installation steps, the rail goes in back end first: the two pegs on its back end piece go into the lowest and highest holes of the chosen U on the rear flange, and the end piece is pushed on until its latch catches; the front end piece is then seated the same way on the front flange. The rack's flanges are a typical 0.74 m apart, longer than the collapsed rail. In the demo both hands carry the rail in level and push its back end home; then one hand lets go and the other draws the front member out along its slide to the front flange, matches it to the same U and pushes it home.
setup: Two YAM arms at the near edge of a table; positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm, heights above the table. A 4-post open-frame rack of black powder-coated steel (shown 29 cm tall, six U of holes) with square-hole flanges (EIA-310: 9.5 mm square holes, three to each 44.45 mm U) stands on the table: its near pair of posts at x 28, the rear flange's inner face at y 37 and the front flange's at y -37 (0.74 m apart); the far pair of posts at x 76. Both near flanges have their third U from the bottom marked with yellow lines (its holes 10.1, 11.7 and 13.3 cm up). A tool-less 1U sliding rail of zinc-plated steel (an 18 x 40 mm channel; 1.35 kg, 0.63 m long collapsed; an outer member with the back end piece, and a front member with the front end piece that slides out along it) lies on the table at (18, 0), along y, its back end toward +y. Each end piece carries two square pegs, at the bottom and top holes of a U, and a spring latch. The arms start at their ready pose.
scoring: Checked by looking at the rail's pegs in the flanges' holes and with a spirit level, as a technician checks. 1.0: both end pieces latched at the marked U (each pushed home on its flange with its two pegs in that U's bottom and top holes), the rail level within 0.5 degrees (its length's angle from horizontal), and every fingertip 3 cm or more from the rail's line (the line through its middle along its length), held 2 s. 0.25: the back end latched at the marked U, without the 1.0 result (this includes a front end latched a U off, a sloping rail). 0 otherwise (a rail hung reversed, its back end at the front flange, scores 0), or if the rail falls after an end piece has latched.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at 240 Hz on GPU. The latches are coded: an end piece whose pegs are both within 1 mm of one U's holes must be pushed past a 10 N detent over its last 3 mm (approximated, to be measured); once home it is held where it seated, as the latch's hook holds it. The pegs are square, tapered from 7.5 to 4.5 mm over 9 mm (the real pegs to measure). Rail mass 1.35 kg (to weigh) and slide friction 3 N (to measure). The rack's far posts and frame are drawn only.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Press each end piece's latch release and lift its pegs out of the flange, slide the front member back until the rail is collapsed, and lay the rail on the table at (18, 0) along y, its back end toward +y, as at the start.
